factual_methodology.summary: Revision 1 resolves the prior blocking attribution error. The Federal Reserve is now described only as reporting elevated inflation and geopolitical uncertainty, while the ECB energy/conflict attribution is kept separate. Previously checked TIC, ICI, gold ETF, Federal Reserve and ECB quantitative claims remain materially unchanged.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Direct thesis-led opening; analytical headings; natural EN and PT-BR localization; no exposed QA/template language; caveats are integrated rather than repeated mechanically; progression runs from capital-flow composition through liquidity, gold and financing conditions to falsifiers.

contextual_depth.summary: Current institutional and market mechanisms are sufficient for a weekly wealth-flow monitor; no ornamental historical section is required.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 Markdown table; 2 explicit charts; 1 causal flow visual; 1 regional transmission map/card in both locales.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: The regional map is a transmission card rather than a coordinate map. Charts use explicitly sourced values and do not imply a complete portfolio decomposition.

revision_delta.summary: Declared qa_rework matches the observed delta: the unsupported joint Fed/ECB energy-shock attribution was removed, the later monetary-tightening paragraph was aligned, and no central numbers, dates, scenarios or conclusion were silently changed.

contrary_evidence: Positive aggregate TIC inflow coexists with a negative adjusted long-term balance, weakening any simple dollar-exit interpretation.
Money-market fund assets fell week on week but remained near $8 trillion, so the weekly decline does not establish broad risk reallocation.
Gold ETF AUM includes valuation effects; physical holdings and net flows are the cleaner demand evidence.
limitations: World Gold Council August figures were not independently re-derived from raw fund-level data in this QA cycle; the report distinguishes flow, holdings and valuation effects.
TIC custodial data cannot precisely identify ultimate ownership by country and should not be read as a complete ownership map.
The first-tranche financing interpretation remains an analytical mechanism, not evidence that higher rates have already caused a measured volume of project cancellations.
notes: Revision 1 approved after targeted re-review of the prior rejection and confirmation that the factual-attribution fix is present in both locales. Public materialization remains the publisher's responsibility.

qa_fixes_applied: Separated Federal Reserve and ECB inflation attribution in both locales
Federal Reserve wording now states only what the September 16 FOMC statement supports: elevated inflation and geopolitical uncertainty
ECB energy-conflict attribution remains explicitly tied to the ECB source
Rechecked the later monetary-tightening section for consistent evidence status

en.title: Global Wealth Flow Monitor — 21 September 2026
en.deck: Dollar liquidity remained central while long-term U.S. securities flows weakened, money-market assets stayed near $8 trillion, gold ETF holdings reached a record and higher policy rates raised the financing hurdle for long-duration investment.
en.regime: High liquidity preference and defensive gold demand coexist with two-way cross-border securities flows as higher policy rates make long-duration financing more selective.
en.key_risk: Persistent energy-linked inflation and higher policy rates could turn a selective financing environment into project delays, credit deterioration and weaker long-term capital formation.
watch: September gold ETF holdings and flows
